caption:
Their avatar talks and waves. Paralysed.
Nature Neuroscience, 14 Sept 2026. Brosler et al., Chang lab, UCSF.

An ECoG implant and machine-learning decoders let paralysed participants speak and gesture, such as nodding and waving, through an avatar at the same time. Three participants, two in real time, restricted vocabulary, wired, in a lab. A demonstration, not a treatment. Which would you want back first, the words or the wave?

#neuroscience #bci #science #neurotech
voiceover_script: Paralysed and unable to speak. Their avatar talks and waves, straight from their brain. This is a brain-computer interface from the Chang lab at UCSF. A high-density implant called ECoG records signals from the brain. Machine-learning decoders turn those signals into speech and into gestures, like nodding and waving, and an on-screen avatar performs both at the same time. Now the honest part. Three participants, two of them driving the avatar in real time, with a restricted vocabulary, over a wired connection, in a lab. This is a demonstration, not a treatment you can go and get.
